No sponsor+location+concrete step for a distinct new facility. Watch for a dedicated re-export/bunkering terminal announcement.

dormant_revival_findings.notes: Cancelled by the National Energy Policy Council; explicitly replaced by the Surat Thani FSRU concept. No independent revival.

dormant_revival_findings.site: Chana LNG Terminal, Chana/Songkhla (KOGAS/Korea Western Power/TPIPP)
dormant_revival_findings.notes: March 2021 KOGAS/KOWEPO/TPIPP MOU for an LNG terminal + Songkhla Chana power station; no updates in 4+ years, inferred cancelled. TPIPP 'Chana Project' page describes an industrial-estate/power plan, not a live marine LNG import terminal. No different-sponsor new project at the site.

dormant_revival_findings.site: Surat Thani FSRU (EGAT/PTT, Phunphin), offshore Surat Thani
dormant_revival_findings.notes: The EGAT+PTT '5 Mt/year FSRU in southern Thailand' feeding the 1,400 MW Surat Thani (Phunphin) power plant IS this shelved record, not a new project. No FID/EPC/land-lease step; no revival beyond the existing shelved concept.

documented_duplicates.candidate: Gulf MTP LNG Terminal (GMTP) / Map Ta Phut Industrial Port Development Phase 3 / MTP3
documented_duplicates.maps_to: Map Ta Phut LNG Terminal 3 (T100000130894, roster #3)
documented_duplicates.why: Same project. Gulf (70%) + PTT Tank (30%) JV, 35-yr PPP with IEAT, initial ~5-8 mtpa expandable to 10.8 mtpa, EPCC signed 2025 (PEC-CAZ / Posco), construction Q4 2025, ops Q1 2029. This is an UPDATE (status proposed->construction, capacity, FID) for the Update workflow, not a Discovery. gem.wiki page 'Gulf MTP LNG Terminal' redirects to Map Ta Phut LNG Terminal 3.
Same shelved EGAT+PTT concept feeding the 1,400 MW Surat Thani/Phunphin power plant; explicitly the replacement for the cancelled Gulf of Thailand FSRU.

out_of_scope_dropped.candidate: Hin Kong Power LNG imports (Gulf + Ratch, 1.4 mtpa shipper licence, Ratchaburi 1,400 MW plant)
out_of_scope_dropped.why_out_of_scope: LNG-shipper licence, not a terminal. First private cargo (Feb 2025) was received at PTT's existing Map Ta Phut 2 / Nong Fab terminal; the Hin Kong power plant is pipeline-fed from that terminal. No new marine facility. Gas turbine plant = GOGPT, not a terminal (Quang-Trach-class).

out_of_scope_dropped.candidate: B.Grimm Power LNG imports (first private importer, feeds 7 small power plants)
out_of_scope_dropped.why_out_of_scope: Shipper licence importing through existing PTT terminals; no dedicated new import facility. Power plants are GOGPT.

out_of_scope_dropped.candidate: Ratch Group / GPSC / Siam Gas & Petrochemical LNG shipper licences
out_of_scope_dropped.why_out_of_scope: ERC has licensed many new LNG shippers 2021-2025, but a shipper licence is not a physical import terminal (they all use MTP1/MTP2). No new-build facility from any of them.

out_of_scope_dropped.candidate: PTT plan to grow LNG portfolio to 15 mtpa; PTTEP Erawan/Bongkot upstream reinvestment
out_of_scope_dropped.why_out_of_scope: Portfolio/volume growth and domestic upstream gas production, not a new terminal. No FLNG/export idea: Thailand is a declining producer + net LNG importer; PTTEP capex only slows the Gulf-of-Thailand decline, no export/liquefaction terminal proposed.

summary: Rings C (sponsor IR) + D (upstream/broader) + gem.wiki cross-check: ZERO new terminals clear the tight bar. The only new physical terminal in Thailand's pipeline is Map Ta Phut LNG Terminal 3 (= Gulf MTP LNG Terminal / MTP3), which is already GEM roster #3 (T100000130894) and now has EPCC + PPP + construction start Q4 2025 -> that is an Update (status/capacity/FID), not a Discovery. All the 2021-2025 'private LNG' activity (Gulf/Ratch Hin Kong, B.Grimm, GPSC, Siam Gas) is LNG-shipper licences importing through existing MTP1/MTP2 terminals -> out of scope (shipper != terminal; the power plants are GOGPT). No FLNG/export idea: Thailand is a declining Gulf-of-Thailand producer and net LNG importer; PTTEP only reinvests to slow field decline. The 'ASEAN LNG hub / re-export' vision runs through existing/planned MTP terminals, not a new facility (1 monitor entry). All 4 dormant sites (Songkhla FSRU, Gulf of Thailand/Samut Prakan FSRU, Chana, Surat Thani FSRU) remain dead with no different-sponsor revival. gem.wiki cross-check: 7 Thai LNG-terminal pages found, all map 1:1 to the roster -> 0 wiki-only gaps. Counts: 0 new_terminals, 1 monitor, 0 gem.wiki gaps, 2 documented duplicates, 4 out-of-scope drops.
